fieldMarks: Toad 40-113 mm, brown, grey or reddish with several dorsal spots and warts; belly greyish with a spotted chest.
High cranial crests with pronounced knobs between and behind the large, protruding eyes distinguish it from the American and Fowler's toads.
Males smaller with darker throats; tadpoles are solid black with a diagonal gold line behind the eye.
behavior: Mainly nocturnal; hides in self-made burrows by day and often feeds under lights near buildings.
Terrestrial until breeding, when it migrates to nearby wetlands; males call during breeding and sometimes in heavy rain at other times.
Eats spiders, beetles, ants and other invertebrates; inactive in the coldest months.
habitat: Wide variety of wooded and unwooded habitats, usually on sandy soil; burrows when inactive; breeds in permanent ponds, woodland pools and flooded depressions.
range: NatureServe lists it in the southeastern US: Virginia, North and South Carolina, Georgia, Florida, Alabama, Mississippi and Louisiana.
